name: University of Duisburg-Essen
description: The University of Duisburg-Essen is a public university in the Ruhr area of North Rhine-Westphalia, formed in 2003 from the universities of Duisburg and Essen. It has more than 37,000 students on its two campuses and a university hospital in Essen.
whyIncluded: The University of Duisburg-Essen is among the 10 universities in Germany most chosen by international students (about 7,800 international students, 21% of more than 37,000, per an aggregator figure), per the FinexisEdu shortlist research of October 2026.

livingCosts.summary: The University of Duisburg-Essen quotes only an older average budget, so this is the German blocked-account requirement of 992 euros a month (11,904 a year), split into rent, food, transport and personal using the average shares of other German universities' budgets.
livingCosts.notes: Rung C. Rung B. UDE International Office 'Key information for incomings' (2024/25) PDF: 'According to the DAAD, a German student has average expenses of EUR 867/month including rent, travel expenses, food, clothing, learning materials, health insurance, telephone, Internet, radio and TV licence fees and recreational activities.' The same page: visa proof of funds EUR 934/month; social contribution 'around EUR 305 each semester' which 'includes a semester ticket for free use of all local public transport'. No itemised figures anywhere on uni-due.de (the 'after admission' page refers to DAAD; the SCIES 'Lebenshaltungskosten' page returns 404), and no Duisburg/Essen sister university in the repo, so the 867 total was split with the Germany shares .56/.28/.01/.15: housing 485.52, food 242.76, transport 8.67, personal 130.05 (health insurance sits inside personal). Excluded: social contribution ~305/semester (semester ticket included in it). Caution: 867 is DAAD's older average; DAAD now quotes EUR 992/month (the blocked-account amount from Sept 2024), so parents should expect roughly 15% more; the rung-C fallback would be 992 split as 555.52/277.76/9.92/148.80. Because the 867 figure is explicitly DAAD's older average, the entry uses the current proof-of-funds amount of EUR 992/month (EUR 11,904/year for 2026, study-in-germany.de and expatrio.com read 2026-10-08) split with the Germany shares .56/.28/.01/.15; UDE's own 867 figure is kept here for reference.

programmes.name: Angewandte Informatik - Schwerpunkte Ingenieur- oder Medieninformatik B.Sc.
programmes.summary: No tuition, including for international students. The figure is only the compulsory semester contribution, which includes a Germany-wide transport ticket. Taught in German.
programmes.notes: No tuition fees: North Rhine-Westphalia's public universities charge none, including for non-EU students, and UDE's fee page lists only the social and student-body contribution. Compulsory fees = Sozial- und Studierendenschaftsbeitrag for winter semester 2026/27, EUR 367.80 x2: mobility contribution (Deutschlandsemesterticket) 226.80 + social contribution (Studierendenwerk) 125.00 + student body 16.00. History (same page): winter 2024/25 EUR 302.40 (ticket 176.40 + 110.00 + 16.00) -> 604.80; winter 2025/26 EUR 349.80 (208.80 + 125.00 + 16.00) -> 699.60. Language of instruction: German. Duisburg campus. Applied computer science (engineering or media informatics). 6 semesters, 180 ECTS (programme page studiengang.php?id=1). Programme name and language from UDE's bachelor's overview (uni-due.de/de/studium/bachelor.php).
